evidence.claim: Caspian Services, Inc. (operating as Caspian Services Group) historically expanded its geophysical capabilities by adding specialized marine seismic source vessels to its fleet to execute state-chartered geophysical survey projects in the Kazakh sector of the Caspian Sea.

The company operates a shallow-draft fleet specifically engineered for the highly restrictive shallow waters of the North Caspian Sea near the Kashagan discovery, providing historical data acquisition support.

Delivery Reliability.assessed_on: While the company has a verified physical and operational presence in western Kazakhstan providing shallow-draft marine seismic source vessel logistics, no secondary research data or case studies exist to verify their precise turnaround times, milestone compliance, or SLA reliability specifically within the advanced data processing and imaging domain.

evidence.claim: Historical financial disclosures via the SEC.gov note that for regional offshore acquisition projects, such as the Oman Pearls field contract for CMOC/Shell, Caspian Services Group sub-contracted the specialized seismic execution to its joint venture partner Veritas Caspian, rather than independently producing client feedback for processing services.

Customer Feedback / Peer Standing.assessed_on: We searched for independent client reviews, peer case studies, or technical client feedback relating explicitly to Caspian Services Group's execution of advanced marine processing routines, but found no external verification, as the company primarily operates as a vessel fleet charterer and subcontracts technical seismic data processing.

evidence.claim: In a Department of Energy research collaboration focusing on the Wind River Basin and Riverton Dome, Echo Geophysical Corporation was designated as the processing provider. They successfully executed a processing stream consisting of true amplitude recovery, surface consistent deconvolution, time-variant spectral whitening, and residual statics.
Historical professional records indicate that Echo Geophysical maintained specialized regional teams, such as a Houston group with staff geophysicists overseeing 3D PSTM reprocessing workflows.

HPC Resourcing & Team Capacity.assessed_on: While historical competencies in time processing and regional basin workloads were verified, there is zero current third-party documentation confirming that Echo Geophysical possesses high-performance computing clusters or specialized teams scaled for heavy FWI or RTM workloads.

evidence.claim: A historical project processing stream executed by Echo Geophysical Corporation for the Riverton Dome 3-D seismic dataset outlined standard workflows but omitted granular milestone benchmarks or delivery durations, as documented by the University of North Texas (UNT) Digital Library.

While historical project tracking files confirm the company executed regional dataset processing, public records via Stretto contain no public performance indicators or verified delivery metrics evaluating execution speed against committed milestones.

Turnaround Time.assessed_on: With no granular milestone benchmarks or delivery durations in the Riverton Dome 3-D processing record from the UNT Digital Library, and no verified delivery metrics in project tracking files via Stretto, Echo Geophysical Corporation is rated at the lower end of the peer range on turnaround; based on primary research, the company has not disclosed its execution speed against committed milestones.

evidence.claim: A self-reported company case study details an "Offshore Seismic Data Processing for Project in Asia" published on October 12, 2025, on the GeoSubsea Case Studies Platform.

Client testimonials from offshore industry professionals like Nguyen Thanh Hoa highlight the firm's execution of integrated Multibeam Bathymetry (MBES), Side Scan Sonar (SSS), and Ultra-High-Resolution Seismic (UHRS) data processing workflows on the official GeoSubsea Portal.

Project Track Record.assessed_on: While the provided evidence confirms GeoSubsea's capability to process high-resolution shallow geophysical datasets for engineering applications, it completely lacks third-party verified evidence or case studies demonstrating large-scale oil and gas exploration projects in complex deepwater, subsalt, or thick sediment environments using advanced workflows like FWI or RTM.

evidence.claim: GeoSubsea states on its official corporate platform that it has "5+ years of combined experience" in marine data processing, utilizing workflows like deghosting and band-pass filtering for Sub-Bottom Profiler (SBP) and Ultra-High-Resolution Seismic (UHRS) datasets.
GeoSubsea claims on its official website to have a global footprint with projects delivered across Asia, Europe, and the Middle East for developers, survey companies, and engineering consultancies.

Global Market Standing & Reputation.assessed_on: The rating rests on GeoSubsea's self-reported 5+ years of combined experience in marine data processing using deghosting and band-pass filtering workflows, and its stated global footprint of projects delivered across Asia, Europe and the Middle East. Based on primary research, the company has not disclosed independent third-party industry recognition.

evidence.claim: GeoSubsea self-reports on their official Marine Survey Data Processing Home Page (https://geosubsea.com/) that they deliver marine data processing and interpretation services for offshore wind, oil & gas, and cable route projects worldwide.

On their Sub-Bottom Profiler & Ultra High-Resolution Seismic Processing page (https://geosubsea.com/sub-bottom-profiler-sbp-ultra-high-resolution-seismic-uhrs-processing/), the company outlines its workflow using tools like RadExPro, Kingdom, and Geosuite to map shallow geological stratigraphy, sediment layers, and geohazards for marine engineering and oil & gas clients.

Relevant Client Portfolio & References.assessed_on: While GeoSubsea states that it has capabilities in processing sub-bottom profiling and ultra-high-resolution seismic data for the oil & gas and offshore wind industries, there is a complete absence of third-party verified project references, named oil majors, or national oil companies demonstrating established market trust.

evidence.claim: Harvex Geosolutions partnered with Shearwater GeoServices to execute a two-month 3D marine seismic survey on blocks OML 100 and OPL 2010 offshore Nigeria on behalf of TotalEnergies EP Nigeria Limited and Matrix Energy, successfully completing the project according to timeline milestones in May 2026.

Harvex Geosolutions, in strategic collaboration with Shearwater GeoServices and the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), successfully completed a two-month multi-client 3D seismic acquisition and onboard processing campaign in the Western Niger Delta Basin utilizing the vessel SW Duchess, wrapping up data collection within the committed window by March 2026.

Delivery Reliability.assessed_on: We verified the company's track record in hitting committed project timelines for specific multi-month offshore data collection and processing campaigns, though explicit internal SLA metrics and third-party audit reports were absent from the public domain, placing the company in a standard, clear capability tier rather than a market-leading one.

evidence.claim: A 2026 joint project completion by Shearwater GeoServices and Harvex Geosolutions successfully finalized a 3D marine seismic survey on blocks OML 100 and OPL 2010 offshore Nigeria for major clients TotalEnergies EP Nigeria Limited and Matrix Energy.

Harvex Geosolutions has executed multiple localized oilfield projects in Côte d'Ivoire, ranging from processing contracts to virtual data rooms, as highlighted during the SIREXE Conference alongside PETROCI and GeoPartners Ltd.

Customer Feedback / Peer Standing.assessed_on: Based on primary research, the company has not disclosed independent client satisfaction metrics, third-party reviews, or score-based peer rankings on delivered processing algorithms; the visible evidence is restricted to vendor announcements and press releases detailing joint exploration partnerships with major international operators.

evidence.claim: In cooperation with Lime Petroleum AS, PSS-Geo executed processing and inversion workflows to produce a "Mega grid" of true amplitude seismic data converted into lithology cubes.

PSS-Geo was explicitly contracted by MultiClient Geophysical ASA (MCG) to conduct the marine seismic processing of the ~8,400 km long MCG1301 2D multi-client survey in the southwestern Norwegian Barents Sea.

Relevant Client Portfolio & References.assessed_on: We verified that PSS-Geo has a proven track record of executing marine seismic processing and reprocessing workflows for multi-client library owners and independent operators (e.g., Lime Petroleum, MCG), but direct, verified references for major international oil & gas majors or global NOCs are less prominent.

evidence.claim: A three-year-long, $13 million dollar R&D project conducted in partnership with an integrated oil and gas company focused on developing algorithms and workflows for seismic, CSEM, and well-log integration, where deliverables and weekly reports were managed through a Technical Steering Committee.

A commercial reservoir property inversion project executed for a Kosmos Energy/Tullow joint venture on the Jubilee Field, offshore Ghana, utilizing rock physics-driven seismic inversion attributes to guide field development decisions.

Turnaround Time.assessed_on: While Rock Solid Images demonstrates a solid track record of completing complex multi-disciplinary reservoir characterization projects, public evidence confirming specific turnaround delivery times in days or weeks against committed benchmarks for standard processing projects could not be verified, placing the company in the unproven category for this exact metric.

evidence.claim: The company maintains a small specialized technical team consisting of five seismic processors with an average of over 20 years of experience executing 2D/3D land and marine processing across multiple continents, as verified by Signature Seismic Processing Inc.'s LinkedIn Profile.

Individual workforce data identifies key team members such as President/Owner Mike Moussallem and Processing Manager Lona Gregory, who utilize commercial third-party platforms like Landmark's SeisSpace and Paradigm's Focus/Echos to execute workflows, as documented in Lona Gregory's LinkedIn Profile.

HPC Resourcing & Team Capacity.assessed_on: Signature Seismic Processing's rating rests on its five-person team averaging over 20 years of 2D/3D land and marine processing experience. Based on primary research, the company has not disclosed specific HPC cluster size or node counts for FWI/RTM-class workloads.

evidence.claim: UGEO Solutions launched "UgeoSeis" as its dedicated in-house seismic data processing division in 2024 to execute broadband deghosting, pseudo-3D processing, and amplitude versus offset analysis.
Public recruitment records indicate active hiring for specialized roles including Senior Seismic Processors and Geophysicists to support regional workloads.

HPC Resourcing & Team Capacity.assessed_on: While the company documents an expanding team of 51–200 employees and an active in-house processing division, the concrete scale of its high-performance computing cluster hardware or cloud infrastructure remains unquantified, placing it in the partial self-reported band.

evidence.claim: UGEO Solutions showcases its specialized "UgeoSeis" in-house division for 2D and 3D marine seismic processing, offering onboard processing and high-resolution broadband site survey workflows.
General marketing material from UGEO Solutions highlights their integrated capabilities designed to process data efficiently.

Turnaround Time.assessed_on: The rating rests on UGEO Solutions' UgeoSeis division, which handles in-house 2D and 3D marine seismic processing with onboard processing and high-resolution broadband site survey workflows.
